name: Russet Green
lede: Russet Green is a moderate greenish yellow that Maerz and Paul trace to 1731, the oldest first-recorded date, and it leans toward Scheele's Green rather than any true russet.

sections.title: An old name, a green that isn't russet
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul date Russet Green to 1731, printed on their plate 20 K 1[1]. The Inter-Society Color Council's 1955 census calls it a moderate greenish yellow, Munsell 0.4GY 6.7/5.9 [1].

Its nearest library neighbor is [[scheele-s-green]], a pigment name, only 2.6 color-distance units away, with [[olive-green]] close behind at 2.9 [1]. Two other greens sit almost as close: [[reseda]] and [[cosse-green]], each within 3.4 units [1]. *Russet* is an old word for a coarse reddish-brown wool, which makes this yellow-green a departure from its own family's usual warmth, something no book in our collection explains [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds Russet Green in 171 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.7 percent, as photographed [2]. It peaks in the 1910s, in 11 of 523 paintings, at three and a half times its average rate, and favors Pointillist and Post-Impressionist hands: Niels Larsen Stevns carries it in 5 of 22 dated works, Georges Seurat in 7 of 41 [2]. Switzerland's painters use it four times the archive's base rate [2]. The counts are a computed color match on varnished, photographed canvases, never a pigment identification [2].

origin.named_after: undocumented; *russet* is an old reddish-brown cloth word
